questions.topic: Hari Singh Meets Anil and Works for Him
questions.stem:
Anil was asleep. A beam of moonlight stepped over the balcony and fell on the bed. I sat up on the floor, considering the situation. If I took the money, I could catch the 10.30 Express to Lucknow. Slipping out of the blanket, I crept up to the bed. Anil was sleeping peacefully. His face was clear and unlined; even I had more marks on my face, though mine were mostly scars.

Choose the option that best explains why the speaker mentions his own scarred face at this moment. (A) admires how different a sleeping face can look (B) sets Anil's unmarked face against his own scarred one (C) checks whether the notes have been hidden somewhere else (D) wonders whether Anil is sleeping as lightly as he appears

answerScheme.modelAnswer: sets Anil's unmarked face against his own scarred one

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Hari Singh Meets Anil and Works for Him
questions.stem:
I couldn’t cook his meals, run to the bazaar or learn to write whole sentences any more. I had forgotten about them in the excitement of the theft. Whole sentences, I knew, could one day bring me more than a few hundred rupees. It was a simple matter to steal — and sometimes just as simple to be caught. But to be a really big man, a clever and respected man, was something else. I should go back to Anil, I told myself, if only to learn to read and write.

Choose the option that best explains the change in the speaker's plan as the night goes on. (A) He decides to hand the notes over to the police instead of Anil (B) He decides to stay in the bazaar until the rain stops (C) He decides to keep the money and leave by the first available train (D) He decides that learning to read and write matters more than the notes

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Hari Singh Meets Anil and Works for Him
questions.stem: Your colony has opened an evening class for young people who work during the day and never went to school, and a boy of fifteen from your own colony has just learnt to write his name after joining it. Write a notice for the colony notice board announcing the class, saying who may join it and requesting volunteers. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the notice gives the purpose of the class (young people who work during the day and never went to school), who may join, when it meets and the request for volunteers
Format: a capitalised heading, the body of the notice in clear short paragraphs, and the signature or designation of the person issuing it at the end
Organisation: the details are arranged in a sensible order, that is, what the class is, who it is for, when it meets, how to join and who may volunteer
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal and concise tone suitable for a notice board
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that persuade young people to join and readers to volunteer

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
COLONY NOTICE BOARD
EVENING CLASS

Residents are requested to note that an evening class will begin in the community hall for young people who work during the day and never had the chance to go to school. The class will meet every evening after working hours and there is no age bar for learning. Boys and girls who wish to join may enrol at the ward office on any working day. Anyone who can read and write is requested to volunteer as a teacher. A boy of fifteen from our own colony could not write his name a month ago and can now add numbers. Please encourage every young person to come forward.

Sd/- Programme Officer

evidence: He also taught me to write my name and said he would
I knew that once I could write like an educated man

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Hari Singh Meets Anil and Works for Him
questions.stem: You read a letter in your local newspaper in which a reader says that learning to read and write is the one thing that can change the life of a poor person. Write your own letter to the editor, in about 100 words, agreeing with this view, giving your reasons and ending with an appeal to readers to teach someone to read and write.

markingPoints.description: Content: the letter agrees with the view that learning to read and write can change a poor person's life, gives reasons and ends with an appeal to readers to teach someone
Format: the correct letter to the editor format, that is, the addressee, the subject line, a greeting, the body and a courteous closing with the writer's name
Organisation: the agreement comes first, followed by the reasons and then the appeal, in clear paragraphs
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a polite, formal tone suitable for a letter to the editor
Expression: short, clear sentences with suitable vocabulary that convince the reader without repetition

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
To: The Editor
Subject: Learning to read and write

Respected Sir,

I read with interest the letter in your paper on how learning to read and write can change the life of a poor person. I fully agree. A boy who cannot write his own name can be cheated easily, as one who cannot add numbers can be cheated on his shopping. A person who can read a whole sentence can stand on his own feet. Whole sentences, he knows, can one day bring him more than a few hundred rupees. I appeal to every reader to teach one person in this locality to read and write.

Yours faithfully,
A Class 10 student

HIRING: TRAINED HANDS, NO QUALIFICATION

A shop in your area will train and employ young people who cannot read or write. No school certificate and no experience are needed. questions.stem:
When I reached the station I did not stop at the ticket office (I had never bought a ticket in my life) but dashed straight to the platform. The Lucknow Express was just moving out. The train had still to pick up speed and I should have been able to jump into one of the carriages, but I hesitated — for some reason I can’t explain — and I lost the chance to get away.

Choose the option that best explains the speaker's hesitation at the platform. (A) He was frightened by the speed the train had picked up. questions.stem:
I found myself in the maidan and sat down on a bench. The night was chilly — it was early November — and a light drizzle added to my discomfort. Soon it was raining quite heavily. My shirt and pyjamas stuck to my skin, and a cold wind blew the rain across my face.

Choose the option that best completes this sentence: The image of the cold wind blowing the rain across the speaker's face shows a thief who is ______. I opened the door quietly, then stood in the doorway, in clouded moonlight. Anil was still asleep. I crept to the head of the bed, and my hand came up with the notes. I felt his breath on my hand. I remained still for a minute. Then my hand found the edge of the mattress, and slipped under it with the notes.

Choose the option that best explains why the speaker remains still for a minute before slipping the notes back. (A) He is waiting for Anil to wake up and ask for the money (B) He is so nervous about being caught that he can hardly move (C) He wants Anil to wake up so that he can confess to him (D) He is counting the notes again to check the amount is right

questions.stem: Trace in steps how the speaker goes from deciding to rob Anil to putting the notes back under the mattress.

Anil had given him a key to the door, so he could come and go as he pleased
He told himself it was time to do some real work, that he was out of practice, and that Anil would waste the money on his friends
He crept up to the bed while Anil slept, drew out the notes and counted 600 rupees in fifties
The Lucknow Express moved out while he hesitated and he lost the chance to get away
In the maidan and the shelter of the clock tower he realised whole sentences could bring more, so he slipped the notes back under the mattress
